title: Research on the physical economy
description: Original studies of land, power, property risk and infrastructure, with public records, methods and downloadable data.

recordHistory.heading: How physical records change over time
recordHistory.description: Compare dated records for a parcel, a commercial mortgage and a highway project. Each example links to the original documents and downloadable data.

examples.title: A tax lot kept its ID after a split
examples.linkLabel: See the tax maps and parcel crosswalk

observations.text: On Brooklyn block 3947, lot 1’s mapped footprint covers about 45,290 square feet.
Lot 1 keeps its ID and about 53% of its former mapped area. The rest becomes lot 105.

examples.title: One refinance, two debt obligations
examples.linkLabel: See the filings and loan history

observations.text: The original Block 40 mortgage has an outstanding balance of $73.6 million, per Stewards’ quarterly filing.
Stewards reports repayment at refinancing. The closing terms list a $69 million restated senior mortgage and a mezzanine loan of up to $10 million.

examples.title: A rejected bid stayed in the project history
examples.linkLabel: See the bid decision and tracker records

observations.text: The Texas Transportation Commission rejects the $2.62 million low bid for work on US 287 in Tarrant County.
TxDOT’s project tracker lists the same project as Ready to Let, with the contractor field empty.

studies.title: When a larger substation pad changes the land test
studies.summary: In a worked example with 56 acres left after constraints, changing the 345 kV utility pad from 8.5 to 16.5 acres creates a 7.5-acre shortfall.
studies.imageAlt: Of 80 gross acres, 56 remain after constraints. The base layout needs 55.5 acres. The layout with a larger utility pad needs 63.5 acres.

studies.title: One building with two energy reports
studies.summary: At 280 Broadway, two city energy reports share a building identifier. The 2025 readings are 112.5 and 55.1 kBtu per square foot, with different reported floor areas.

studies.title: How two $415 million records are linked
studies.summary: At 25 Water Street, a rent assignment points directly to the agreement recorded the same day. The public record chain shows how a lender can reconcile both entries.
studies.imageAlt: Aerial view of 25 Water Street in Lower Manhattan with the tax lot outlined.

studies.title: What a $232.5 million site purchase included
studies.summary: Core Scientific allocated $227.8 million of its $232.5 million Hunt County purchase to development rights. In a separate Oklahoma deal, it disclosed a $40 million payment tied to delivery of additional firm power.

studies.title: One feeder, three capacity figures
studies.summary: In Vail Mills, National Grid reported 3.18 MVA of summer load headroom, 4.98 MVA in winter and 0.10 MW of solar export capacity.

studies.title: Eight buildings share one address
studies.summary: Appanoose County’s 2021 property schedule lists 12 building and contents entries across eight building IDs at one address. Match each line to the building before reconciling reported values or valuation terms.

studies.title: Two points in the same hailstorm
studies.summary: Two Denver points shared the same annualized FEMA rate and the same coarse radar tile. The finer radar estimates for the storm were 1.42 and 0.55 inches.

studies.title: How a Brooklyn tax lot changed
studies.summary: A split kept the original tax lot number while changing its shape. Seven dated geometries show how to reconstruct the boundaries before and after the changes.

studies.title: When a watershed crosses a county line
studies.summary: Four watersheds appeared in both county queries for Loudoun and Fairfax. Join by watershed and month before using the results in a water availability review.

studies.title: Count charging ports at a highway exit
studies.summary: Two stations near an Ohio interchange show why counting equipment rows can misstate the number of ports available to drivers.
